{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A defines its product, buyer and price hypothesis ($15-20/mo individual, ~$200/mo team, anchored to Depot's $20/mo plan). Idea B's own brief says the description is unconfirmed and the customer 'varies by idea', so there is nothing concrete to sell within 90 days.",
    "Idea A's demand evidence comes from several independent, linked sources across HN, Reddit and LinkedIn. One quantifies cost (~$43k/year in waiting) and one states willingness to pay ('Solve this and I would pay for it'). Idea B has one post seeking a builder, and the same thread rebuts the premise.",
    "Idea A's competitors show real usage (act at 72k stars) and multiple shipped MVPs, which confirms the need and that a solo founder with agents can build it. Idea B's competitors show no traction, and at least two display dummy or illustrative data, which points to weak underlying demand.",
    "Idea B's core need (non-coders needing humans to build prototypes) is undercut by vibe-coding tools, as users in its own evidence say. Idea A's pain persists despite those tools: environment parity remains a real problem.",
    "Idea A has a plausible path to a paid wedge through team or hosted features with a known price anchor. Idea B's only paid comparable (CoFoundersLab) sits in an adjacent category and carries a billing-practice class-action flag."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's demand evidence rests on a single Reddit post seen through a third-party mirror ('Looking for someone to make apps with...'), and the same thread argues the need no longer exists ('you can just vibe code'). Its acquisition-cost estimate ($100-200 per paying customer) comes from a vendor blog the brief itself labels 'not independently verified'.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A wins mainly because B is undefined and thinly evidenced, not because A is proven. A has a serious unresolved risk: about seven free OSS competitors and zero confirmed paid conversion in the category, so reaching a paying customer within 90 days depends on finding a team or hosted feature developers will pay for. Neither brief shows price validation in its exact category."
}
